title: Customer booking widget (service pick -> slot pick -> book -> confirmation)
tech: React + TypeScript + Vite, consumes the existing REST API (GET /services, GET /availability, POST /bookings) -- no new backend endpoints, one small backend touch for CORS
keyConstraints: TypeScript strict, no customer accounts/login anywhere in this flow (guest checkout only, matching the established design decision), API base URL configurable via env, not hardcoded
description: First frontend task -- this is what makes the product launchable, since right now booking only works via raw HTTP calls. Scope is the new-booking flow only: browse services, pick a date/slot, submit the booking form, see a confirmation screen. The customer's magic-link manage page (view/cancel/reschedule an existing booking, from task 007's API) is deliberately out of scope here -- separate follow-up task, same slicing discipline the backend used (booking creation was task 001, customer self-management was a separate task 007). Explicit assumption, flag for Architect to confirm: there's no existing frontend scaffold in this repo -- backend lives at the repo root (src/, package.json). Add a new top-level web/ folder as a sibling to src/, with its own package.json/vite config, rather than restructuring the existing backend into a subfolder -- avoids touching nine tasks' worth of established backend paths for a cosmetic reorganization. Three backend-interaction details worth getting right, all directly tied to work already done on the backend: (1) GET /availability returns slot start times as UTC ISO strings for display in the customer's own browser-local timezone (per the design doc's non-functional section) -- but the exact UTC string must be passed through unmodified to POST /bookings's start_at, never reformatted or reconstructed client-side, to avoid any lossy round-trip through a different timezone library or string format; (2) POST /bookings can return 409 when someone else books the same slot in the gap between the customer viewing availability and submitting -- this is the concurrency protection from task 001 working as intended, not an error state to hide, so the UI needs a specific 'that slot was just taken' path that re-fetches availability, not a generic error message; (3) a successful POST /bookings returns status: pending, not confirmed -- the confirmation screen must say the request is awaiting the masseur's review, not imply the booking is final, matching the actual manual-confirmation semantics built in task 002.
acceptanceCriteria: Customer can view active services (name, price, duration) fetched from GET /services
Selecting a service and a date shows available slots fetched from GET /availability?service_id&date, displayed in the customer's browser-local timezone -- not UTC, not the provider's timezone
Submitting the booking form calls POST /bookings with the exact UTC start_at string originally returned by GET /availability for the selected slot, unmodified
On success, the customer sees a screen that clearly states the request is pending the masseur's confirmation -- not a final 'you're booked' message
On a 409 response, the customer sees a specific 'that slot was just taken' message and the available slots are re-fetched, not a generic/raw error

Client-side validation on the booking form (name, email format, phone format) mirrors the backend's requirements for immediate feedback, understood as a UX nicety -- the backend remains the sole source of truth
The submit button is disabled or shows a loading state while the request is in flight, preventing accidental double submission
The API base URL is read from an environment variable, not hardcoded, so the same build can target different backend deployments
The Express backend has CORS configured to allow the frontend's configured origin specifically (env-driven allowlist), not a wildcard -- the one backend file touched in this task
No login, signup, or account concept appears anywhere in this flow
securityConsiderations: CORS must allow only the configured frontend origin, never a wildcard, since the API also serves authenticated admin routes -- an overly permissive CORS policy would widen the attack surface for those even though this task's own flow is unauthenticated. No customer PII is stored client-side beyond what's in the form during submission (no localStorage of name/email/phone). Rely on the backend's existing input validation and rate limiting -- this task adds client-side validation for UX only, not as a security control.
